To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cardiac ET system is activated and contributes to LV dysfunction that gradually occurs in compensated LVH in Ren-2 rats.
activation of the cardiac ET-system impairs LV function in renin-dependent hypertension via decreased sarcoplasmic Ca2 uptake.

activation of the cardiac ET-1 system accounts at least partly for the LV dysfunction in LVH and that ETA receptor antagonists can improve LV diastolic dysfunction by normalizing the impaired SR Ca2 uptake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ET system in LVH and its transition toward heart failure in Ren2 rats.
the role of cardiac ET-1 and the ET receptor subtypes in the pathogenesis of hypertension and LVH and the development of cardiac dysfunction in this model of hypertension.
the role of the endothelin system in left ventricular hypertrophy (LVHT) and the transition to heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activation of the cardiac ET-1 system in Ren2 rats is responsible for the transition from compensated LVH to LV dysfunction, which is associated with a reduction of SR Ca2+ transport.
the cardiac endothelin system is involved in the development of left ventricular dysfunction in renin-dependent hypertension via decreased sarcoplasmic Ca2 uptake.
activation of the cardiac endothelial system impairs left ventricular function in renin-dependent hypertension via decreased sarcoplasmic Ca2 uptake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of the cardiac ET receptor subtype A is responsible for the transition from compensated LVH to cardiac dysfunction in Ren2 transgenic rats.
activation of the cardiac ET-1 system is a major factor in the transition of compensated LVH to LV dysfunction.
the ET system contributes to the development of LV dysfunction in LVH.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cardiac endothelin system plays an important role in the transition of LV hypertrophy to LV dysfunction and that the selective ET subtype A receptor antagonist Lu135253 may be a promising therapeutic strategy for this condition.
the cardiac ET system plays a pivotal role in the development of LV dysfunction in Ren2 rats.
ETA antagonism can improve LV dysfunction and prevent LV remodeling in the setting of LVH.
